title: Bats May Have First Evolved in Europe 65 Million Years Ago
summary:
New research suggests that bats most likely originated in Europe during the late Paleocene, roughly 65 to 60 million years ago. For decades, researchers have debated where bats first appeared, and Africa, Asia and North America have all been proposed as possible birthplaces.

An international team of 137 researchers from 64 countries combined genomic data from every living bat family with evidence from ancient fossils. Their goal was to reconstruct the evolutionary history of the world's only mammals capable of true powered flight. The work was carried out through the Bat1K consortium, a global effort to sequence the genomes of all living bat species. The study, published in Nature, examined 103 bat genomes, including 42 newly generated chromosome-level assemblies, covering all 21 recognized bat families. The researchers also used evidence from 44 fossil bats.

The results suggest that bats first evolved in Europe and that their descendants then moved into Africa. As bats diversified, separate groups expanded into the Americas, Asia and Australia. Over time, those migrations produced the major bat lineages found around the world today.

The findings also offer clues about two defining bat features. The team analyzed the fossil bat Vielasia, which sits on the oldest branch of the bat family tree. That fossil suggests that echolocation, the use of sound to navigate and hunt in darkness, had already appeared close to the beginning of bat evolution. Taken together, the evidence indicates that both powered flight and echolocation emerged before modern bat groups began diversifying.

Professor Emma Teeling, the leading senior author and a co-founding director of Bat1K, said: "we finally have a robust phylogenetic tree that we can now use to properly understand how and where bats' unique traits evolved." Senior author Professor Liliana M. Dávalos of Stony Brook University said the team's method can "identify the oldest group of fossil bats while taking the genomic data into account."

Bats represent about one fifth of all living mammals and play important ecological roles around the world. Many species are unusually resistant to disease and can live far longer than other mammals of similar size.
why_it_matters: A reliable bat family tree gives scientists a map for studying how traits like flight, echolocation and unusual resistance to disease developed.

questions.question: Which continents have been proposed as bat birthplaces in the past?
options: Antarctica, Australia and Africa
Africa, Asia and North America
South America and Antarctica only
Europe and Australia only

questions.question: What kinds of evidence did the team combine?
options: Satellite photos and weather records
Genomic data from living bat families and fossils
Written histories and old maps of caves
Sound recordings and pictures of bat wings
questions.correct_answer: Genomic data from living bat families and fossils

questions.question: How many recognized bat families did the 103 genomes cover?
options: Only 4 of the bat families
All 21 recognized bat families
About half of the bat families
Just one family of fruit bats

questions.question: According to the study, where did bats' descendants move after Europe?
options: Into the Americas, and nowhere else
Into Asia, and then they stopped spreading
Straight to Australia, then back to Africa
Into Africa, and later other groups spread elsewhere
questions.correct_answer: Into Africa, and later other groups spread elsewhere

questions.question: What does the evidence indicate about powered flight and echolocation?
options: Both emerged before modern bat groups began diversifying
Echolocation came late, and flight never evolved
Both appeared only after modern bat groups formed
Flight came late, and echolocation never evolved
questions.correct_answer: Both emerged before modern bat groups began diversifying

questions.question: What did Liliana M. Dávalos say about the team's method?
options: It can identify the oldest group of fossil bats while using genomic data
It replaces the need to study any living bat species
It works only when scientists have no fossils to study
It proves that bats are older than every other mammal
questions.correct_answer: It can identify the oldest group of fossil bats while using genomic data

background_read: A genome is the complete set of DNA in a living thing. Sequencing a genome means reading it letter by letter.
